## Publications

::: {.paper}
[**[Trapped by Tradition: Gender and Occupational Segregation in Peru](https://doi.org/10.1093/sp/jxaf039)**]{.ptitle}<br>
[with Arlette Beltrán, María Amparo Cruz-Saco and Favio Leiva]{.coauthors}<br>
[*Social Politics: International Studies in Gender, State & Society*, 2025 · [doi:10.1093/sp/jxaf039](https://doi.org/10.1093/sp/jxaf039)]{.pmeta}

[Using nearly two decades of census and household survey data, we document that
occupational segregation in Peru persisted even after women surpassed men in
educational attainment, and that marriage and motherhood are associated with a
higher likelihood of segregation.]{.pabstract}
:::

## Under review

::: {.paper}
[**Never Off Duty: Grandmothers' Co-residence and Mothers' Labor Participation**]{.ptitle}<br>
[with Arlette Beltrán, María Amparo Cruz-Saco and Sebastián Núñez Rosell]{.coauthors}<br>
[Revise and resubmit, *Social Politics*]{.pmeta}

[Comparing mothers who live with a grandmother to those who do not, we find the
former are more likely to work and to hold better-quality employment, suggesting
that informal intergenerational caregiving substitutes for absent public
childcare.]{.pabstract}
:::

::: {.paper}
[**[Does Scarcity Tax Parents' Minds?](https://bfi.uchicago.edu/working-papers/does-scarcity-tax-parents-minds)**]{.ptitle}<br>
[with Ariel Kalil]{.coauthors}<br>
[BFI Working Paper 2026-46 · Under review, *Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics*]{.pmeta}

[Low-income parents spend less time than advantaged parents on educational activities
with their children, and a common explanation is that financial scarcity imposes a
bandwidth tax on cognition. Surveying 1,932 mothers of kindergartners in Chicago
Public Schools, we ask whether the binding constraint is attention or self-control,
and whether the cost comes from low income itself or from the subjective experience
of not having enough. Attentional capacity, not self-control, is the primary
constraint, and felt scarcity rather than household income predicts attentional
deficits.]{.pabstract}
:::

::: {.paper}
[**[A Novel Assessment of Epistemic Curiosity and its Association with Early Learning Outcomes](https://bfi.uchicago.edu/working-papers/a-novel-assessment-of-epistemic-curiosity-and-its-association-with-early-learning-outcomes/)**]{.ptitle}<br>
[with Ariel Kalil, Dana McCoy, Michelle Michelini and Terri Sabol]{.coauthors}<br>
[BFI Working Paper 2026-112 · Under review, *Child Development*]{.pmeta}

[We develop and validate the Animal Game, a ten-trial behavioral task that measures
epistemic curiosity in young children and can be administered in the field rather
than the laboratory. In a socioeconomically diverse sample of 594 U.S. children aged
three to six, the task yields a novelty score and a knowledge-seeking score, with
high internal consistency and measurement invariance across child sex and parental
education.]{.pabstract}
:::

## Working papers

::: {.paper}
[**[Income Shocks and the Intergenerational Transmission of Executive Function](https://bfi.uchicago.edu/working-papers/income-shocks-and-the-intergenerational-transmission-of-executive-function/)**]{.ptitle}<br>
[with Ariel Kalil]{.coauthors}<br>
[BFI Working Paper 2026-30]{.pmeta}

[Using Baby's First Years, a randomized trial of unconditional cash transfers to
low-income mothers, we study the transmission of executive function from mothers to
their four-year-old children.]{.pabstract}
:::

## Work in progress

::: {.paper}
[**Preschool Absenteeism and Experimental Sign-Up Bias: Evidence from a Field Experiment across U.S. States**]{.ptitle}<br>
[with Sebastián Gallegos, Ariel Kalil and Ritika Sethi]{.coauthors}

[A randomized field experiment across eight U.S. states testing whether a low-cost
behavioral intervention reduces chronic absenteeism in early childhood. We build a
new dataset linking daily administrative attendance records to parent surveys for
2,048 children in 49 Head Start centers. Opt-out recruitment enrols 98 percent of
eligible families, which also lets us measure how volunteer recruitment shifts the
estimated treatment effect. Pre-registered as AEARCTR-0014680.]{.pabstract}

[**Presented at** EC*REACH, Northwestern · Chicago, June 2026 — From Research to Action Convening, Attendance Works and the Overdeck Family Foundation · New York, July 2026 — Advances with Field Experiments, Becker Friedman Institute · Chicago, September 2026]{.pmeta}
:::

::: {.paper}
[**How Traditional Are We? Gender Roles, Household Tasks, and Women's Labor Force Participation in Peru**]{.ptitle}<br>
[Single-authored]{.coauthors}
[Drawing on the 2024 round of Peru's National Survey of Social Relations, which
introduces the first nationally representative battery of gender-role attitudes, I
find that stronger traditional attitudes correlate with lower labor force
participation among women, and that the unequal division of household tasks accounts
for part of that association.]{.pabstract}

[**Presented at** Annual Congress of the Peruvian Economic Association · Lima, 2026]{.pmeta}
:::

## Other writing

::: {.paper}
[**Perú sin tiempo: la otra cara de la pobreza**]{.ptitle}<br>
[with Arlette Beltrán, Pablo Lavado and Sebastián Núñez Rosell]{.coauthors}<br>
[Research report, Universidad del Pacífico Research Centre · September 2025]{.pmeta}

[Using Peru's 2024 Time Use Survey, we estimate that 29.6 percent of Peruvians are
time poor, above the 27.9 percent who are income poor, and that the burden falls
hardest on women, on rural households and on adults between 31 and 65.]{.pabstract}

[**In the press** [CIUP](https://ciup.up.edu.pe/analisis/arlette-beltran-pablo-lavado-peru-sin-tiempo-la-otra-cara-de-la-pobreza/) · [*Infobae Perú*](https://www.infobae.com/peru/2025/09/09/peru-sin-tiempo-la-otra-cara-de-la-pobreza/) · [*El Comercio*](https://elcomercio.pe/opinion/colaboradores/ser-pobre-de-tiempo-por-arlette-beltran-y-pablo-lavado-la-pobreza-de-tiempo-en-el-peru-noticia/)]{.pmeta}
:::
